title: Small Signs of Respect Tell People You Honor Relationships
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece catalogs small, deliberate gestures of respect as a low-cost, high-impact way to build trust in new or uncertain relationships. The author argues these gestures matter disproportionately because they function as a signal of how someone sees the other party, especially before deeper trust has been established through longer acquaintance. Alongside common courtesies like eye contact and attentive listening, the piece lists several less obvious gestures — such as accepting a 'No' immediately without pushback, or ignoring small faux pas — as markers used by especially skilled relationship-builders.
points: Small gestures of respect matter most in new relationships, where they substitute for the trust that hasn't yet been built through time.
The respect we extend to others functions as a lens into how we see ourselves, according to the piece's framing.
Less obvious respect gestures — accepting a 'No' without discussion, ignoring minor faux pas, never turning your back mid-conversation — distinguish especially skilled relationship-builders.
The true measure of a person is offered as how they treat others who can do nothing for them.
quotes: Small signs of respect between people go a long way in establishing a positive and mutually influential relationship.
Giving respect through small gestures says more about who we are to others than just about any other act or disclosure.
The respect we offer others is always a lens into how we see ourselves.
The true measure of a person is how they treat others who can do nothing for them.
Immediately accepting any 'No' without discussion or reaction
Incorporating distinctive signs of respect into our everyday styles as leaders and people helps us forge the deepest relationships.
